tone_statements.citation: Ebarb, Kristopher J; Green, Christopher R; Marlo, Michael R. 2014. Luyia tone melodies. Africana Linguistica 20: 121-143.
tone_statements.quote: Luyia languages manifest a microcosm of the three major types of tonal systems found in Bantu: ‘ conservative’, ‘ predictable’, and ‘ reversive’, classifications which describe synchronic tonal properties of verb roots and the distribution of inflectional tonal melodies (Marlo 2013b). ... In predictable languages like Khayo and Tura, all verb roots are underlyingly / Ø/. As in other predictable tone systems in Bantu (Odden 1989), all verbs have a tense‑determined tonal suffix ... [p.123] Luyia tonal melodies are among the most numerous and complex in Bantu; we count 11 melodies in Khayo and Marachi.
tone_statements.summary: Khayo is a 'predictable' Bantu verbal tone system: no lexical tone contrast in verb roots (all toneless), tone on verbs comes from tense/aspect/mood/polarity-determined melodic H tones (a tonal suffix realized on stem positions), with 11 distinct inflectional melodies in Khayo; framework is privative H vs zero with the mora as counting unit; no statement about word stress or accent.

tone_statements.citation: Marlo, Michael R. 2009. Khayo verbal tonology. Africana Linguistica 15: 77-129. DOI 10.3406/aflin.2009.1003 (Persée).
tone_statements.quote: Khayo has only one underlying tone: H; other tone-bearing units are underlyingly toneless. There is a surface contrast between level H and level L on short and long vowels … L is the ‘ default tone’, i. e. the automatic phonetic implementation of phonological Ø … Falling and rising tones are found on long vowels as combinations of H and Ø … require the mora to be the tone-bearing unit in Khayo … Khayo has automatic downstep of non-adjacent Hs … Khayo has a ‘ predictable’ tone system that lacks lexical tonal contrasts in verb roots.

tone.says: One underlying tone, H vs toneless (surface H vs L; long-vowel contours are H+Ø sequences); mora is the TBU; automatic downstep only; verb roots lack lexical tone, tense-assigned melodic Hs mark TAM.
